{{nihongo|'''Mononobe Shrine'''|物部神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Tsutsui|Q62588744|qid=Q62588744|lt=Tsutsui}}, {{ill|Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Q578824|qid=Q578824|lt=Higashi-ku}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It has been identified with "Mononobe Shrine" of Aichi District, Owari Province, in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' but as noted below, there are differing views. {{nihongo|'''Mononobe Shrine'''|物部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== History ==
It is an old shrine with a tradition of founding in the era of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, and is said to have once had broad precinct grounds. With a large stone as {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}, it was called '''Ishigami-dō''' or '''Yama-no-Kami''' until the {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}}. The '{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}' compiled around the mid-{{ill|17th century|Q7016|qid=Q7016}} records "Furui Village ... Yama-no-Kami," suggesting it was worshiped as a mountain deity at that time. In the {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} era, {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunanari|Q982743|qid=Q982743}} is said to have repaired the dilapidated shrine buildings<ref name="立て板"/><ref name="由緒記"/>.

The large stone called "Kaname-ishi," treated as sacred object, is said to be under the shrine building, with a legend that {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}} used it to pacify the {{ill|Country|Q6256|qid=Q6256}} when subduing this area.

In the Edo period, {{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} identified this shrine as the Owari Aichi District "Mononobe Shrine" listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' and this became the prevailing view. However, his basis was only that its deity was {{ill|Umashimaji|Q10946169|qid=Q10946169|lt=Umashimaji-no-Mikoto}}, ancestral deity of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}, and no materials such as {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} survive. Late-Edo local historian {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} criticized identifying this shrine as Mononobe Shrine and argued the original Mononobe Shrine was {{ill|Gokiso Hachimangū|Q3109957|qid=Q3109957}}. Archaeologically, few ancient remains are found around this site, whereas around {{ill|Gokiso|Q50984787|qid=Q50984787}} kofun and abandoned temple sites are scattered; therefore, the theory identifying Mononobe-gō in Aichi District of the '{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}' with the Gokiso area is considered stronger{{Sfn|名古屋郷土文化会|1986|p=5}}.
